Over the years, the Commission has frequently been called upon to make individual determinations of the size of specific commercial zones, and a number of economic and social factors have been deemed relevant to such determinations, Commercial Zones, 124 M.C.C. at 138. Use of these and similar factors to distinguish between local urban transportation which should be exempt under section 203(b)(8) and linehaul movements which are subject to our regulation will yield much more useful results. Our inquiry will undertake to relate these characteristics of exempt commercial zone operations to the economic evidence of record, the objectives of the National Transportation Policy, and public interest considerations. The scope of the exemption should be interpreted so as not to vitiate the benefits of motor carriage.
An analysis of section 203(b)(8) reveals that an area must meet two requirements if it is to be included within a commercial zone - it must be (1) "adjacent to" and (2) "commercially a part" of the base municipality. The first requirement implies some type of reasonable geographic 16 proximity. Consequently, this precludes inclusion of areas geographically remote from the base municipality, even though there may be intense economic interaction between the remote area and the base municipality.
